survivors.claim: review-legs.js summary destructures readManifest(manifest) with no null guard; an absent manifest at that point raises a bare TypeError ('Cannot destructure property byLeg of null') instead of a message naming the file. Pre-image threw an equally unnamed ENOENT from readFileSync, so this is not a regression, but the new reader's null contract makes a one-line named refusal cheap.
survivors.impact: If the manifest vanishes mid-run the operator sees a stack trace rather than a sentence naming the missing file.
survivors.evidence: Hunk: `const { byLeg } = readManifest(manifest)`; lib/manifest.js returns null when the path cannot be read (spec Contracts). No test exercises this path; advisory only.

survivors.claim: verdict.js's cannot-read refusal dropped the underlying error message (`: ${e.message}`) when the inline loader was replaced by readManifest, so ENOENT vs EACCES are no longer distinguishable on stderr. The remedy sentence ('confirm the evidence manifest was created') is retained, so the host's error-path rule is still met.
survivors.impact: A permissions failure on the manifest now reads the same as a missing file.
survivors.evidence: Diff hunk removes `: ${e.message}` from the console.error; readManifest swallows the caught error and returns null. No test pins e.message (grep 'cannot read --manifest' tests -> only escalate-row.test.js:69, which asserts its absence).
